title: Handling Numeric Expressions in Automatic Speech Recognition
claim: Numeric-expression formatting (years, timestamps, currency, quantities) is context dependent; cascaded vs end-to-end formatting compared with LLM+TTS adaptation data; LLM approaches strong, adapted E2E competitive at lower cost.
not_covered: Transcript-level formatting only; no executed tool call, no silent-wrong cell, no pipeline vs audio-native comparison, no confirmation lever.

title: Digits micro-model for accurate and secure transactions
claim: Financial multi-digit number recognition: a specialised micro-model reaches 1.8% digit error vs 5.8% for Whisper on diverse real-world digit-string speaking styles.
not_covered: ASR digit error rate only; no downstream call, no pipeline or acoustic grid, no confirmation.

title: Mind the Gap: Entity-Preserved Context-Aware ASR Structured Transcriptions
claim: Whisper-class ASR struggles with named entities and numerical data needing formatting; overlapping context windows and entity-labelled training improve NER and entity formatting.
not_covered: ASR-side fix scored on NER/formatting; nothing downstream, no tool calls, no acoustic grid, no lever.

title: Retrieval Augmented Correction of Named Entity Speech Recognition Errors
claim: RAG-like LLM correction of rare entity-name ASR errors using a vector DB of entities; 33-39% relative WER reduction on voice-assistant music queries without regressing on STOP.
not_covered: Corrects names via a known catalogue; amounts, digits, dates have none; no executed ledger, no audio-native arm, no confirmation.

title: RECOVER: Robust Entity Correction via agentic Orchestration of hypothesis Variants for Evidence-based Recovery
claim: Agentic entity correction using multiple ASR hypotheses (1-best, entity-aware select, ROVER, LLM-select) plus retrieval; 8-46% relative entity-phrase WER reduction, up to +22 pp recall over five datasets.
not_covered: n-best used for correction, not as a clarification gate; scored by E-WER/recall, not executed-call semantics; no pipeline or acoustic comparison.

title: ContextASR-Bench: A Massive Contextual Speech Recognition Benchmark
claim: 40k-entry, 300k+ named-entity benchmark across 10+ domains with context-exploitation modes; LALMs outperform conventional ASR by a large margin on entities.
not_covered: Entity recognition of the transcriber only; domain terms not amounts/digits/dates; no tool calls, no silent-wrong labelling, no confirmation.

title: Contextual ASR Error Handling with LLMs Augmentation for Goal-Oriented Conversational AI
claim: Ranks n-best ASR hypotheses by dialogue-state context and context by phonetic match; correction recall +34%, F1 +16% with real users in two domains; users rate higher when correction works.
not_covered: Correction inside an assistant, not a measurement of executed-wrong calls; no audio-native arm, no acoustic grid, no read-back lever.

title: An approach to measuring the performance of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models in the context of Large Language Model (LLM) powered applications
claim: Argues WER misweights ASR error types once an LLM is the downstream consumer; analyses LLM error correction and proposes a new ASR measure for LLM-powered applications.
not_covered: Metric proposal; no tool-calling agent, no entity-error isolation, no pipelines or acoustic conditions, no lever.

title: Perceptually Better, Semantically Worse: Measuring Speech Enhancement Impact on LLM-Based Voice Systems
claim: Output Divergence Rate on 2,974 SLURP clips with Whisper/wav2vec2 cascades: enhancement can double intent divergence despite better PESQ; echo yields speaker substitution WER cannot capture; audio metrics weakly predict ODR.
not_covered: Intent classification not tool arguments; divergence not partitioned into silent-wrong vs surfaced vs asked; no audio-native arm, no confirmation lever.

title: Performant ASR Models for Medical Entities in Accented Speech
claim: Across 93 African accents, models with low overall WER still show higher clinical-entity error (patient-safety risk); introduces medical NE recall, medical WER, CER; fine-tuning improves medical WER 25-34% relative.
not_covered: Entity error on transcripts, never executed; accent is the only condition; no LLM downstream, no pipelines, no confirmation.

title: Beyond WER: Entity and Disfluency Recall in Accented Conversational ASR
claim: WER-optimised ASR misses named entities in accented English (recall 53-55%); entity-dense curation plus regional LoRA on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B reaches 80-85% recall; six-category error taxonomy with LLM judge.
not_covered: Names not amounts/digits; no downstream action or tool call; no telephone band or noise; no confirmation.

title: Analyzing Error Propagation in Korean Spoken QA with ASR-LLM Cascades
claim: Downstream degradation from ASR errors is consistent across LLMs (tracks ASR information loss); single-character errors salient; a large audio LM beats a matched-backbone cascade in noisy Korean SQA.
not_covered: QA not tool calls; no entity-type ledger, no silent-vs-asked partition, no confirmation lever; its cascade-vs-native result cuts against our D2 and must be cited.

title: Measuring the Effect of Transcription Noise on Downstream Language Understanding Tasks
claim: Configurable framework for evaluating task models under transcript-noise severities and types and transcript cleaning; models tolerate some noise and react differently to error types.
not_covered: Text-side noise on summarisation-style SLU tasks; no spoken entities, no executed calls, no pipeline comparison, no confirmation.

title: Back to Basics: Revisiting ASR in the Age of Voice Agents
claim: WildASR factorises ASR robustness along environmental degradation, demographic shift and linguistic diversity in four languages; seven ASR systems degrade unevenly and hallucinate plausible unspoken content under degraded input, a safety risk for downstream agents.
not_covered: Stops at the transcript; agent risk asserted not measured as executed calls; no entity breakdown, no pipelines, no confirmation lever.

title: Responsible ASR: Overcoming Challenges of Foundational Models in Narrow-Band and Low-Resource Settings
claim: Foundation ASR (open and commercial) is suboptimal zero-shot on narrow-band telephony Hindi and Indian-accented English customer-support calls; fine-tuning helps unevenly.
not_covered: WER on telephony audio only; no entity analysis, no LLM or tool call, no controlled wide-vs-narrow comparison, no confirmation.

title: Learning ASR-Robust Contextualized Embeddings for Spoken Language Understanding
claim: Confusion-aware fine-tuning makes pre-trained LM representations similar for acoustically confusable words from word confusion networks, improving SLU on ASR transcripts.
not_covered: Pre-LLM slot/intent SLU; no tool execution, no entity ledger, no audio-native arm, no lever.

title: ASR-GLUE: A New Multi-task Benchmark for ASR-Robust Natural Language Understanding
claim: Six NLU tasks under ASR error across 3 noise levels and 6 speakers; studies noise intensity, error type and speaker effects; correction and augmentation help only partly.
not_covered: NLU classification, not slot values feeding an action; no LLM tool calling, no telephone band, no confirmation.

title: SLURP: A Spoken Language Understanding Resource Package
claim: Large diverse English SLU dataset (18 domains) with NLU+ASR baselines and a transparent entity-labelling metric enabling detailed error analysis.
not_covered: Labels on transcripts; no execution, no silent-wrong concept, no LLM tool calling.

title: STOP: A Dataset for Spoken Task Oriented Semantic Parsing
claim: Largest public spoken semantic-parsing dataset with human and TTS audio and low-resource splits, motivated by avoiding cascading ASR errors.
not_covered: Parse accuracy; no executed calls, no entity-type ledger, no LLM comparison, no confirmation.

title: SpokenWOZ: A Large-Scale Speech-Text Benchmark for Spoken Task-Oriented Dialogue Agents
claim: 249 h human-human spoken TOD; cross-turn and reasoning slots; best DST 25.65% JGA and best E2E completes 52.1% of requests, ChatGPT included.
not_covered: DST not tool execution; slot errors not split into surfaced vs silent; no audio-native LLM with tools, no acoustic grid, no confirmation.

title: Speech-based Slot Filling using Large Language Models
claim: GPT-3.5/GPT-4/LLaMA/Vicuna on slot filling over noisy ASR transcripts of SLURP at several ASR error rates; prompt design plus linearised knowledge injection gives +8.3 SLU-F1.
not_covered: Slot F1 on transcripts; no executed call, no silent-vs-asked partition, no audio-native arm, no confirmation.

title: Revisit Input Perturbation Problems for LLMs: A Unified Robustness Evaluation Framework for Noisy Slot Filling Task
claim: Noise-LLM: five single and four mixed perturbations for slot filling with augmentation and demonstration strategies; open LLMs show limited robustness.
not_covered: Text perturbations, not audio; slot extraction, not execution; no pipelines, no acoustic grid, no lever.

title: Towards ASR Robust Spoken Language Understanding Through in-Context Learning with Word Confusion Networks
claim: Feeding LLMs word confusion networks from ASR lattices in ICL narrows the gap to oracle transcripts on spoken QA and intent classification across ASR conditions.
not_covered: n-best used to improve answers, not to decide whether to ask; no tool execution, no entity ledger, no audio-native arm, no confirmation.

title: Towards interfacing large language models with ASR systems using confidence measures and prompting
claim: Confidence-based filtering decides which ASR transcripts an LLM corrector may touch, improving weaker ASR systems without damaging good transcripts.
not_covered: Confidence gates a corrector, not a clarification; WER-scored; no tool calls, no entities, no pipeline comparison.

title: Adopting Whisper for Confidence Estimation
claim: Whisper fine-tuned to emit word-level confidence matches or beats confidence-estimation-module baselines in and out of domain.
not_covered: Confidence quality only; no gating experiment, no entities, no tool calls, no downstream decision measured.

title: Proactive for Uncertainty: Cause-Aware Error Diagnosis and Interactive Clarification for Spoken Dialogue Systems
claim: Plain ASR confidence filtering misses deletions and cannot separate acoustic from linguistic mismatch; small detectors on ASR latents classify token errors and drive targeted multi-turn clarification; recall 57.96% vs 23.66%, up to -30% WER and +17% downstream across accents and distortions.
not_covered: No read-back confirmation arm; downstream metric is not an executed-tool-call ledger split into silent-wrong / surfaced / asked; no audio-native arm; no entity-type breakdown; no asked-when-right cost.

title: The Cascade Equivalence Hypothesis: When Do Speech LLMs Behave Like ASR->LLM Pipelines?
claim: Matched-backbone testing plus logit-lens/LEACE show the transcript emerging inside speech LLMs; in most uses they are expensive cascades and under noise worse ones, clean advantages reversing by up to 7.6% at 0 dB.
not_covered: General accuracy, not tool-argument semantics; no silent-vs-asked partition; no confirmation lever.

title: Spoken Function Calling: A New Perspective on Spoken Language Understanding for Large Audio Language Models
claim: Reframes SLU as spoken function calling; builds SFC-Bench from SLU datasets via a multi-agent synthesiser; evaluates LLMs and LALMs and post-trains LALMs; SFC beats traditional SLU on semantic extraction.
not_covered: No partition into schema-valid-wrong vs surfaced vs clarified; calls not executed against a backend; no acoustic grid; no confirmation or confidence lever.

title: From Text to Voice: A Reproducible and Verifiable Framework for Evaluating Tool Calling LLM Agents
claim: Converts text tool-calling benchmarks (Confetti, When2Call) to paired audio with TTS, speaker variation and noise; 7 omni-modal models; text-to-voice gap 1.8-4.8 points; degradations mostly reflect misunderstood argument values in speech.
not_covered: Omni-models only (no Whisper cascade or audio-LLM-transcriber arm); argument errors not tabulated as a silent-wrong ledger by entity type; gold-label scoring not executed no-error-no-question criterion; no telephone band, rate or per-accent spread; no confirmation, gating or instruction lever; no WER covariate.

title: MTVA-Bench: Evaluating the Language Model Inside Cascaded Voice Agents
claim: Evaluates the LM inside a cascaded voice agent with LLM-played callers, transcription issues, and a mock backend responding to the arguments actually sent; 490 scenarios, 7 languages; tool selection similar across models but overall scores span 24.4 points, mostly argument values, ordering and rule compliance.
not_covered: Text-simulated transcription issues, no real audio, no acoustic conditions, no audio-native arm; argument errors not traced to a mis-heard entity or split into silent-wrong vs asked; no confirmation or confidence lever.
